title: Octagons of Salim Chishti’s tomb (Fatehpur Sikri)
subtitle: Tomb of Salim Chishti, Fatehpur Sikri

given.O: The centre of the tile, where four pieces turn round one point like a pinwheel.
given.A: A corner of the large octagon round O, halfway to the next tile’s centre.

construction.note: The finished design was read from Wichmann’s SM27 drawing, whose pieces are drawn edge to edge. O is the centre of the four pieces that turn round the middle of the tile, and OA is half the repeat. Every edge runs at a multiple of 22.5° and lies on one of a few lines: the sides of the octagon in the circle through A (drawing 0.9238 from O, cos 22.5° = 0.9239), the sides of a smaller octagon through P (drawing 0.6681, tan 33.75° = 0.6682), where P is the centre of the circle inside the triangle OAS3, and the horizontal, vertical and 45° lines through P and its turns (drawing 0.2557, 0.2557 exactly). The four pinwheel pieces round O lie on the 22.5° lines through O. The drawing gives no steps; we devised the construction.
construction.changes: The compass steps, their order and the named points are ours. Wichmann’s page gives the symmetry as p4m, but the four pieces round the centre of the tile turn without a mirror, so the design is a pinwheel; we follow the drawing. His thick and thin bands (the two levels of the design) are drawn as plain lines. Colours follow the shapes, not his drawing, which is one colour. No photograph was checked.

credits.source: Tiling Search, data206/SM27: Tomb of Salim Chishti, Fatehpur Sikri
credits.creator: Brian Wichmann
credits.note: Read from his finished drawing, not construction instructions. His references are David Wade’s photo IND 0820 and a photo by Richard Henry, both of Salim Chishti’s tomb, Fatehpur Sikri (1571).

steps.text: Draw a horizontal straight line through O and A. Draw a circle with centre O through A.

Draw a vertical line through O. It crosses the circle at S5. Draw the line through O that halves the angle between the horizontal and the vertical line. It crosses the circle at S3. Draw a line through O at 90° to it. Draw the line through O that halves the angle between the horizontal line and the line through S3. It crosses the circle at S2. Turn this line round O by 45°, three times. The lines through O cross the circle at S1 to S16, with S1 at A.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: Draw a vertical line through O. It crosses the circle at S5. Draw the line through O that halves the angle between the horizontal and the vertical line. It crosses the circle at S3. Draw a line through O at 90° to it. Draw the line through O that halves the angle between the horizontal line and the line through S3. It crosses the circle at S2. Draw a line through O at 90° to the line through S2.

steps.text: Join S1, S3, S5, S7, S9, S11, S13 and S15 with straight lines. They make an octagon.
Draw the line through A that halves the angle between the horizontal line and the octagon’s side through S3. It crosses the line from O to S2 at P.
Draw a line through P at 90° to the line from O to S2. Turn it round O by 45°, seven times. These eight lines make a smaller octagon.
Draw a horizontal line through P. Draw a line through P parallel to the line from O to S3. Turn the two new lines round O by 90°, three times.
Draw a vertical line through A. Turn it round O by 90°, three times. The four lines make the square tile, with corners K1, K2, K3 and K4.
Join K1, K2, K3 and K4 to mark the tile that repeats.

ink.text: Ink the lines picked out in orange. They close the octagons, the stars between them and the pieces round O.

pattern.text: Put copies of the square tile side by side. The large octagons touch at the middles of the tile’s sides.
